head: `5f54e912` carries every change below; the commit after it changes only this body's source under `pr_bodies/`. On top of main `8a6594be`: 3 commits, 15 files, 296 lines added and 2 removed, measured with `git diff --shortstat`. A draft of the Z239 fix lane, not before the 6.2.0 tag and not for landing before it (owner answer 4 of handover 3).
came_from: Z225 handed the in-toto export of 6.1.0 to five foreign readers (tools/intoto_external on the measurement branch `claude/intoto-external`, commit `13d8faaa60ec1f2d133d94bcea015965cb43a9c7`) and found five things, F1 to F5. The owner answer of 2026-09-26 made them a fix lane after the 6.2.0 tag, and Nachtrag 9 item 2 of 2026-09-27 ordered it: fix each with a failing test first, and where a finding is a limit of a foreign tool rather than our defect, say so and document it instead of bending the format.
defect:
One of the five is ours. The in-toto envelope layer says a keyid SHOULD be included for each signing key (in-toto/attestation v1.2.0, spec/v1/envelope.md), and no DSSE envelope of this package carried one. securesystemslib 1.5.1 raised `KeyError: 'keyid'` in `Envelope.from_dict`, and GUAC 1.1.0 stopped at "failed to find key from key providers" before it read the statement. The class is wider than the in-toto export: `dsse.sign_envelope` signs every DSSE envelope of this package except the trust pack's, which already names its keys.

The other four are what a tool does with a statement the in-toto rules allow. F1: the top-level `contentRootAlg` is an extension field ("Producers MAY add extension fields to any JSON object"; "Consumers MUST ignore unrecognized fields"); the default strict parse of both bindings and cosign refuse it. F2: the test-result payloadType is one of the two forms spec/v1/envelope.md allows, pinned by SPEC section 7b as a type-confusion defense; cosign takes only the other one. F4: GUAC files a statement of a predicate type it does not model as ITE6 and has no parser for it. F5: `cosign verify-attestation` matches the subject against an image digest, and only the release-gate profile names an image.
fix: `dsse.sign_envelope` writes the signer's OpenSSH SHA256 fingerprint as the keyid when none is given (`dsse.openssh_sha256_keyid`, the RFC 8709 wire form hashed), the form go-securesystemslib's `dsse.SHA256KeyID` derives and sigstore's key providers compare. A given keyid is written as it is, and `keyid=""` writes none. The keyid is not signed; `dsse.verify_envelope` and the Rust `verify-dsse` read only the signature, so no verdict and no exit code changes. The agent-review conformance vectors are regenerated by their generator and carry the keyid, one line per signature. F1, F2, F4 and F5 are recorded in `docs/IN_TOTO_PROFILE.md`, section "Reading the export with foreign tools", with the tool version, the in-toto rule and what a reader can do; the format does not change for them.

not_changed:
No verdict and no exit code of either verifier; `SPEC.md` and the test-result payloadType; the in-toto statements and their `contentRootAlg`; the trust pack's own keyids. The keyid names a key and proves nothing: it is not signed, and a relying party still selects the key by its own trust material. Where GUAC is concerned, a signature it verifies still reaches no graph node, because it has no parser for these predicate types.

NOT MEASURED: a second version of any foreign tool; cosign with a transparency log or keyless signing; GUAC with a backend other than the in-memory keyvalue store.
